docs.title: RingCentral MCP Servers
docs.text: Welcome to the developer documentation for RingCentral's Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. These servers expose RingCentral platform capabilities — telephony data, CRM integrations, and more — as structured tools that any MCP-compatible AI client (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.) can call directly.

docs.title: 🔧 RingCentral Labs MCP
docs.text:
URL: https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com

Experimental platform tools built by the RingCentral Labs team. Ideal for prototyping and developer exploration.

View server →

docs.title: 🔗 App Connect (Unified CRM)
docs.text:
URL: https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp

Bridges RingCentral telephony with your CRM platform. Sync call logs, look up contacts, and manage CRM records from any AI assistant.

View server →

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text:
The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI models communicate with external tools and data sources over a well-defined JSON-RPC interface. Each MCP server advertises a list of tools — typed function signatures with names, descriptions, and parameter schemas — that an AI client can discover and invoke.

AI Client  ──────── tools/list ──────────▶  MCP Server
           ◀──── tool definitions ────────
           ──────── tools/call ──────────▶
           ◀────── tool result ───────────

RingCentral's MCP servers let AI assistants take real actions — fetching call records, finding contacts, logging activity — without requiring custom integrations for every AI product.

New to MCP?

Start with the Quickstart guide to connect your first server in under 5 minutes.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: RingCentral MCP servers use a two-layer authentication model. This page explains how each layer works and how to troubleshoot common auth issues.

docs.title: Layer 1 — RingCentral identity
docs.text: All tools require an active RingCentral session. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 via your existing RingCentral account.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: When you connect an MCP server to your AI client, the client initiates an OAuth handshake with RingCentral. You'll be redirected to RingCentral's login page, and upon success, the client receives a session token that is automatically passed with every tool call.

docs.title: Token lifecycle
docs.text:
Token Lifetime Refresh Access token 60 minutes Automatic (silent) Refresh token 7 days Requires re-authentication

If your refresh token expires, you'll need to re-authenticate by disconnecting and reconnecting the server in your AI client's integration settings.

docs.title: Layer 2 — CRM connection
docs.text: Tools marked ⚠️ REQUIRES CRM CONNECTION additionally require a linked CRM account. This is a separate OAuth flow with your CRM provider.

docs.title: Supported CRM platforms
docs.text:
• Salesforce
  • HubSpot
  • Zoho CRM
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 (beta)

docs.title: Connecting a CRM
docs.text:
Via Claude.aiVia App Connect Portal
  1. In a conversation, ask: "Connect my Salesforce account to RingCentral"
  2. The assistant will guide you through the App Connect portal
  3. Complete the Salesforce OAuth login
  4. Return to the conversation — the assistant will confirm the connection
  1. Go to app.ringcentral.com → App Connect
  2. Click Add CRM Integration
  3. Choose your CRM platform
  4. Authorize with your CRM credentials
  5. Return to your AI client — the connection will be active

docs.title: Verifying CRM connection
docs.text:
Check my session status.

Look for "crmConnected": true and the crmPlatform name in the response.

docs.title: RingCentral
docs.text:
Your RingCentral account needs the following permissions for full functionality:

Permission Required for ReadCallLog rcGetCallLogs ReadAccounts getSessionInfo

docs.title: CRM (Salesforce example)
docs.text: Object Permissions Contact Read, Create Task / Activity Read, Create

docs.title: "Authentication failed" on CRM tools
docs.text:
Your CRM session may have expired. Run:

Disconnect my CRM and reconnect it.

Or call logout then re-authenticate via the App Connect portal.

docs.title: "Insufficient permissions" error
docs.text: Your RingCentral account or CRM user role may lack required permissions. Contact your RingCentral or CRM administrator to grant the permissions listed above.

docs.title: OAuth redirect not completing
docs.text:
• Ensure pop-ups are not blocked in your browser
  • Try authenticating from the App Connect portal directly rather than through the AI client
  • If using Claude Desktop, authentication may need to be completed in a browser window

SSO environments

If your RingCentral account uses SSO (SAML/OIDC), the OAuth flow will redirect through your identity provider. Complete the SSO login as normal — the token exchange happens automatically afterward.

docs.title: Connecting to Claude
docs.text: This guide covers how to connect RingCentral MCP servers specifically to Anthropic's Claude products: Claude.ai and Claude Desktop.

docs.title: Claude.ai (web & mobile)
docs.text: Claude.ai supports MCP servers through the Integrations settings panel.

docs.title: Adding a server
docs.text:
1. Open claude.ai and sign in
  2. Click your avatar → Settings
  3. Navigate to Integrations
  4. Click Add integration or Connect more tools

  5. Enter the server URL and a display name:

    Field Value Name RingCentral App Connect URL https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp

  6. Click Connect

  7. Complete the RingCentral OAuth flow if prompted

docs.title: Using tools in a conversation
docs.text:
Once connected, Claude will automatically have access to the server's tools. You can invoke them naturally:

"Look up Jane Smith in my CRM and log a call saying we discussed the Q3 renewal."

To see which tools are available, ask:

"What RingCentral tools do you have access to?"

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text: Claude Desktop uses a local JSON config file to register MCP servers.

docs.title: Config file location
docs.text: OS Path macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Linux ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "rc-app-connect": {
      "url": "https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp",
      "transport": "sse"
    },
    "rc-labs": {
      "url": "https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com",
      "transport": "sse"
    }
  }
}

After saving, restart Claude Desktop for the changes to take effect.

docs.title: Verifying the connection
docs.text: In a new Claude Desktop conversation, look for the 🔌 Tools indicator in the input bar. Click it to see connected servers and available tools.

docs.title: Tools not appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the server URL is correct (no trailing slash)
  • Restart the client after config changes
  • Check that your network allows outbound HTTPS to *.ringcentral.com and *.labs.ringcentral.com

docs.title: Authentication errors
docs.text:
• Re-authenticate: go to Settings → Integrations → disconnect and reconnect the server
  • Ensure your RingCentral account has the necessary permissions (see Authentication)

docs.title: CRM tools returning errors
docs.text:
• Call getSessionInfo to check CRM connection status
  • If crmConnected: false, re-link your CRM from the App Connect portal

Tip

If you're evaluating MCP for your team, the Quickstart guide has the fastest path to a working demo.

docs.title: CRM Integration Workflow
docs.text: This guide walks through the most common real-world workflow: automatically logging RingCentral call activity into your CRM using AI.

docs.title: Workflow 1 — End-of-day call logging
docs.text:
Log all of today's calls to your CRM in one step.

Prompt: 

Log all of my RingCentral calls from today to Salesforce. 
For each call, look up the caller in the CRM and attach the log to their record.

What happens under the hood:

  1. rcGetCallLogs — fetches today's calls
  2. For each call record:
  3. findContactByPhone — resolves the caller to a CRM contact
  4. createCallLog — posts the activity with incomingData + contactId

docs.title: Workflow 2 — Inbound caller identification
docs.text:
Identify a caller and surface their CRM record before you pick up.

Prompt: 

Someone is calling from +1 415 555 0123. Who is it and what's their latest CRM activity?

What happens:

  1. findContactByPhone("+14155550123") — returns name, company, CRM URL
  2. AI summarises their record and recent notes

docs.title: Workflow 3 — Post-call note with summary
docs.text:
After a call, dictate a note and have it logged automatically.

Prompt: 

I just finished a call with Jane Smith. 
Log it to Salesforce with this note: 
"Discussed Q3 renewal. She's interested in upgrading to Enterprise. 
Will send proposal by Friday."

What happens:

  1. findContactByName("Jane Smith") — resolves CRM ID
  2. rcGetCallLogs (last 1 hour) — finds the matching call record
  3. createCallLog — posts log with incomingData + contactId + note

docs.title: Workflow 4 — Unknown caller → create and log
docs.text:
Handle calls from contacts not yet in your CRM.

Prompt: 

I just got a call from +1 650 555 9999 — a new prospect named Alex Johnson. 
Create them as a contact in Salesforce and log the call with note: 
"First inbound inquiry. Interested in Team plan."

What happens:

  1. findContactByPhone("+16505559999") → empty result
  2. createContact({ phoneNumber: "+16505559999", newContactName: "Alex Johnson" })
  3. rcGetCallLogs — fetches the call record
  4. createCallLog — logs against the new contact

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Always run getSessionInfo at workflow start to confirm both RC and CRM sessions are active before attempting write operations.
  • Batch by day, not by week — rcGetCallLogs has a 7-day max window. Daily logging avoids hitting limits.
  • Include a note — structured notes make CRM records far more useful than raw telephony data alone.
  • Use incomingData for accuracy — passing the raw RC call record via incomingData.logInfo ensures duration, direction, and timestamps are correctly populated.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Error Likely cause Resolution Authentication failed CRM session expired Call logout then reconnect Contact not found Phone number not in CRM Use createContact first Duplicate log Same call logged twice Check CRM for existing activity before calling createCallLog Invalid phone format Number not in E.164 Prefix with + and country code

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Get connected to a RingCentral MCP server in under 5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A RingCentral account (free developer accounts available at developers.ringcentral.com)
  • An MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, or Windsurf

docs.title: Step 1 — Choose a server
docs.text: Goal Server Log calls to a CRM, look up contacts App Connect Explore experimental RingCentral tools RC Labs MCP

docs.title: Step 2 — Add the server to your AI client
Step 3 — Verify the connection
docs.text:
Once connected, ask your AI assistant:

Check my RingCentral session status.

You should see your RingCentral username and CRM connection status returned.

docs.title: Step 4 — Connect your CRM (App Connect only)
docs.text:
If you're using App Connect and want to sync call logs or look up contacts:

  1. Ask: "What CRM platforms can I connect?"
  2. The assistant will list available connectors
  3. Follow the OAuth flow to link your CRM account

Or see the full Authentication guide.

docs.title: Step 5 — Try your first tool
docs.text:
Show me my RingCentral call logs from today.

Look up the contact "Jane Smith" in my CRM.

Log my last call with Jane Smith to Salesforce with the note: discussed renewal.

You're set up!

Explore the Tool Reference for all available tools, or follow the CRM Integration Workflow guide for a real-world automation example.

docs.title: Servers Overview
docs.text: RingCentral currently publishes two MCP servers. Both implement the Model Context Protocol specification and are reachable over HTTPS using Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport.

docs.title: Server registry
docs.text: Server URL Status Tools RingCentral Labs MCP https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com 🟡 Labs / Beta — App Connect (Unified CRM) https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp 🟢 Available 9

docs.title: Transport & protocol
docs.text:
Both servers use SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport over HTTPS, which is the recommended transport for remote MCP servers. Clients connect by sending an HTTP POST to the server URL with a JSON-RPC 2.0 body.

# Discover tools on any server
curl -X POST https://<server-url> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'

docs.title: Authentication model
docs.text:
• RingCentral Labs MCP — no authentication required for tool discovery; some tools may require a valid RingCentral session.
  • App Connect — tools marked ⚠️ REQUIRES CRM CONNECTION require the user to have authenticated with both RingCentral and a supported CRM platform. See Authentication.

docs.title: Versioning policy
docs.text: Labs servers follow a rolling-release model. Breaking changes will be announced in the Changelog with at least 14 days notice. Stable tools are versioned via api-version query parameter where applicable.

docs.title: App Connect (Unified CRM)
docs.text: Endpoint: https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp Status: 🟢 Available Transport: SSE over HTTPS Tools: 9

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The App Connect MCP server bridges RingCentral telephony with your connected CRM platform. It enables AI assistants to look up contacts, create CRM records, and sync call activity — all through natural language.

Supported CRM platforms include Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, and others supported by the RingCentral App Connect product.

docs.title: Connecting
Authentication
docs.text:
This server uses a two-layer auth model:

  1. RingCentral identity — required for all tools. Uses OAuth 2.0 / SSO via your RingCentral account.
  2. CRM connection — required for tools marked ⚠️ REQUIRES CRM CONNECTION. Users must link their CRM account via the App Connect portal.

See Authentication guide for step-by-step setup.

docs.title: Tool summary
docs.text: Tool CRM Required Description getSessionInfo — Current user identity and CRM connection status getPublicConnectors — List available CRM connectors getHelp — Quick integration guide findContactByName ⚠️ Search CRM contacts by name findContactByPhone ⚠️ Search CRM contacts by phone number createContact ⚠️ Create a new CRM contact createCallLog ⚠️ Log a call activity to the CRM rcGetCallLogs ⚠️ Retrieve call logs from RingCentral logout — Sign out from the CRM session

docs.title: RingCentral Labs MCP
docs.text: Endpoint: https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com Status: 🟡 Labs / Beta Transport: SSE over HTTPS

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The RingCentral Labs MCP server is the experimental home for new platform capabilities built by the RingCentral Labs engineering team. Tools published here are under active development and subject to change.

Labs status

Tools on this server are not covered by RingCentral's standard SLA. They may be renamed, modified, or removed without prior notice. Use in production with caution.

docs.title: Connecting
Tool discovery
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
The Labs MCP server roadmap includes upcoming tools for:

  • RingCentral AI Noise Cancellation — expose transcription and noise-cancel status
  • Analytics & Reporting — pull QoS and usage metrics for a RingCentral account
  • Video Meetings — create, list, and summarize RingCentral Video meetings
  • SMS & Messaging — send and receive SMS programmatically

Follow the Changelog for release announcements.

docs.title: createCallLog
docs.text:
Creates a single call activity log in the connected CRM platform. Can accept a raw RingCentral call log record (from rcGetCallLogs) or manually supplied fields.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description incomingData object — A complete RingCentral call log record. Pass items from rcGetCallLogs directly here — no field mapping needed. contactId string — CRM contact ID to associate the log with. contactType string — Type of the CRM contact object (e.g. "Contact", "Lead"). Required by some CRMs when contactId is set. note string — Free-text note or call summary to attach to the log entry.

At least one parameter recommended

All parameters are technically optional, but a useful log entry typically needs at least incomingData or contactId + note.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Field Type Description logId string ID of the created CRM activity record crmUrl string \| null Deep link to the log entry in the CRM UI

docs.title: Example
Recommended workflow
docs.text:
The most complete log entry combines data from rcGetCallLogs with a contact lookup and a human-written note:

1. rcGetCallLogs       → get raw call record
2. findContactByPhone  → resolve CRM contact ID
3. createCallLog       → post log with incomingData + contactId + note

See the CRM Integration Workflow guide for a full walkthrough.

One log per call

This tool creates one log entry per invocation. To log multiple calls, call it once per record from rcGetCallLogs.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected.

docs.title: createContact
docs.text:
Creates a new contact record in the connected CRM platform. Returns the newly created contact's CRM ID and details.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description phoneNumber string ✅ Phone number in E.164 format, e.g. +14155551234 newContactName string — Full name of the new contact. If omitted, the contact is created with only a phone number.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
The created contact object:

Field Type Description id string CRM record ID of the new contact name string \| null Name as stored in the CRM phone string Phone number as stored crmUrl string Deep link to the new record in the CRM UI

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• The phoneNumber field must be in E.164 format. Use + followed by country code and number, no spaces or dashes.
  • Duplicate detection is handled by the CRM platform. If a contact with that phone number already exists, the CRM may return an error or the existing record depending on your CRM's settings.
  • After creating a contact, the returned id can be passed directly to createCallLog.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected.

Related tools

  • findContactByPhone — check for existing contacts before creating
  • createCallLog — immediately log a call against the new contact

docs.title: findContactByName
docs.text:
Searches the connected CRM for contacts whose name matches the provided string. Returns contact details including phone numbers, email, and CRM record IDs.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description name string ✅ Full or partial name to search for (e.g. "Jane", "Jane Smith")

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An array of matching contact objects:

Field Type Description id string CRM record ID name string Full name phone string \| null Primary phone number email string \| null Primary email address company string \| null Associated company or account name crmUrl string \| null Deep link to the record in the CRM UI

Returns an empty array [] if no matches are found.

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• Search is case-insensitive and supports partial matches.
  • If multiple contacts match, all are returned. The AI client is responsible for disambiguation.
  • Use the returned id as the contactId parameter when calling createCallLog.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected. Call getSessionInfo first to verify.

Related tools

  • findContactByPhone — search by phone number instead
  • createContact — create a contact if none is found
  • createCallLog — log a call against the found contact

docs.title: findContactByPhone
docs.text:
Searches the connected CRM for a contact matching the given phone number. Ideal for automatic caller lookup when an inbound call arrives.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description phoneNumber string ✅ Phone number to search for. Accepts E.164 format (+14155550123) or local formats — the server normalises before searching.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An array of matching contact objects (same schema as findContactByName):

Field Type Description id string CRM record ID name string Full name phone string \| null Primary phone number email string \| null Primary email address company string \| null Associated company or account name crmUrl string \| null Deep link to the CRM record

Returns an empty array [] if no match is found.

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• Phone number normalisation handles common formats: (415) 555-0123, 415-555-0123, +1 415 555 0123.
  • When no contact is found, consider calling createContact to add them.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected.

Common workflow

Inbound call → findContactByPhone → display contact info → after call ends → createCallLog

See the full CRM Integration Workflow guide.

docs.title: getHelp
docs.text:
Returns a quick-start guide describing what the App Connect integration can do and how to get started. Useful as an onboarding prompt when a user first connects the server to their AI client.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A plain-text or markdown guide covering:

  • What App Connect does
  • How to authenticate with a CRM
  • A summary of available tools and common workflows

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• This tool is safe to call before authentication is complete.
  • Intended for use at session start or when a user asks "what can you do?"

Related tools

  • getSessionInfo — check current auth status
  • getPublicConnectors — list connectable CRMs

docs.title: getPublicConnectors
docs.text:
Returns the list of CRM connectors publicly available through App Connect. Use this to show users which CRM platforms they can link to their RingCentral account.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An array of connector objects:

Field Type Description id string Unique connector identifier name string Human-readable CRM platform name logoUrl string URL to the connector's logo image authType string Authentication method ("oauth2", "apikey", etc.) status string Availability status ("available", "beta", "deprecated")

docs.title: Example
getSessionInfo
docs.text:
Returns the current user's RingCentral identity and their CRM connection status. Use this tool to verify a session is active before calling tools that require CRM authentication.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A session object containing:

Field Type Description rcUserId string RingCentral user ID rcUserName string Display name of the authenticated RC user rcExtension string RC extension number crmConnected boolean Whether a CRM platform is linked crmPlatform string \| null Name of the connected CRM (e.g. "Salesforce") crmUserId string \| null User ID in the CRM system

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• If crmConnected is false, calls to CRM-dependent tools will return an authentication error.
  • Use this as a health-check at the start of automated workflows.

Related tools

  • getPublicConnectors — see which CRM platforms are available to connect
  • logout — end the CRM session

docs.title: logout
docs.text:
Signs the current user out of the connected CRM platform. The RingCentral session remains active; only the CRM link is severed.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A confirmation object:

Field Type Description success boolean true if the CRM session was successfully terminated message string Human-readable status message

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• After calling logout, tools that require CRM authentication will return an error until the user reconnects.
  • To reconnect, the user must re-authenticate via the App Connect portal or the AI client's integration settings.
  • This does not log the user out of RingCentral itself.

Related tools

  • getSessionInfo — confirm logout was successful

docs.title: rcGetCallLogs
docs.text:
Fetches call log records from the RingCentral platform for the authenticated user within a specified time range. Records can be passed directly to createCallLog without field mapping.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description timeFrom string ✅ Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format, e.g. 2025-05-01T00:00:00Z timeTo string ✅ End of the time range in ISO 8601 format, e.g. 2025-05-06T23:59:59Z

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An object containing a records array. Each record is a complete RingCentral call log object:

Field Type Description id string Unique call log ID sessionId string Session ID (groups legs of the same call) startTime string ISO 8601 timestamp when the call started duration number Call duration in seconds type string "Voice", "Fax", etc. direction string "Inbound" or "Outbound" result string "Accepted", "Missed", "Voicemail", etc. from object Caller info: { phoneNumber, name, extensionNumber } to object Callee info: { phoneNumber, name, extensionNumber } recording object \| null Recording metadata if available

docs.title: Example
Passing records to createCallLog
docs.text:
Each item in records[] can be passed directly as incomingData.logInfo to createCallLog — no field renaming required:

// Use records[0] directly
{
  "name": "createCallLog",
  "arguments": {
    "incomingData": { "logInfo": <records[0]> },
    "contactId": "0031g00000XxYyZAAZ",
    "note": "Call summary here"
  }
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Maximum date range is 7 days per request. For longer ranges, make multiple calls with sequential windows.
  • Results are ordered by startTime descending (most recent first).
  • Calls from all devices and extensions under the authenticated account are included.

CRM connection required

This tool requires an active RingCentral session. The user must be authenticated via RingCentral OAuth.

Related tools

  • createCallLog — write fetched records to your CRM
  • findContactByPhone — resolve caller identity from from.phoneNumber
